title: Bea 'sy valley mooar
description: Ten columns from a weekly paper about life in a big Manx town: a dessert shop with an old oven, the day Illiam Dhone is remembered, a theatre review from the gallery, a tunnel under the promenade pavement, the aquarium by the harbour, an old printer and a calligrapher, a day in the hospital chaplaincy, fireworks night and a frightened dog, an interview with a punk singer who now runs a still, and a council debate on renewing the market.

lessons.title: Yn shapp milljagyn er y straid vooar
lessons.summary: The columnist visits a new dessert shop on the main street in Douglas: Lowenna Trebilcock bakes in an old oven at five each morning, greases her boards with butter so the dough does not stick, tops her best dessert with honeycomb from a beekeeper near the town, sells a salty honey dessert and lemon sweets made with citric acid, writes every label by hand, smiles at every customer, and makes a birthday dessert for a little girl.
lessons.text:
Dagh shiaghtin, ta mee screeu 'sy cholloo shoh mychione bea 'sy valley mooar. Er y Jesarn shoh chaie, hie mee dys shapp noa er y straid vooar ayns Doolish. She shapp milljagyn eh. Ta Lowenna Trebilcock jannoo milljagyn ayn dagh laa, as t'ee creck ad rish sleih y valley.

Ta oghe mooar ayns cooyl y shapp. Ta Lowenna girree ec queig er y chlag, as t'ee cur yn oghe er roish shey. “Ta'n oghe shoh shenn,” dooyrt ee dou, “agh t'eh ny share na oghe noa erbee. T'eh freayll y çhiass dy mie, as cha nel eh losht y teayst.”

Ren ee soilshaghey dou kys t'ee jannoo teayst. T'ee cur flooyr, eeym, ooh as beggan ushtey cooidjagh, as t'ee obbraghey yn teayst lesh e laueyn rish feed minnid. “Smarr ny claareyn lesh eeym hoshiaght,” dooyrt ee, “ny bee'n teayst lhiantyn orroo.” Moghrey elley, smarree ee ny claareyn reesht.

Ta'n milljag share eck jeant lesh shelleig. Ta Lowenna kionnaghey shelleig veih fer ta freayll shellanyn er thalloo beg faggys da'n valley. Ta'n shelleig lane dy vill. T'ee giarey yn shelleig ayns ayrnyn beggey, as t'ee cur ad er mullagh y milljag.

Ta milljag elley eck ta sollanagh as millish ec y traa cheddin: t'ee cur beggan sollan er y vill. “Ta ny paitçhyn gra nagh vel milljag sollanagh kiart,” dooyrt ee, “agh ta ny ayraghyn as ny moiraghyn kionnaghey eh dagh laa.” Ren mee blass y ghoaill. Va'n milljag sollanagh feer vie.

T'ee jannoo millshanyn limon myrgeddin. Ta soorid kidragh ayns limon, as t'ee cur beggan soorid kidragh elley ayns ny millshanyn. Ta'n soorid cur blass geyre daue, as s'mie lesh ny paitçhyn ad.

Ta mynjeig er dagh milljag 'sy uinnag. Ta Lowenna screeu yn ennym as y prios er dagh mynjeig lesh e laue hene. Ta mynjeig gra neesht my vel croiyn ayns y milljag, son dy vel croiyn olk da paitçhyn ennagh.

Ta Lowenna mongey rish dagh kionneyder ta çheet stiagh. “Cha nel monney argid ec sleih nish,” dooyrt ee. “Ta mee laccal dy bee ad sonney tra t'ad faagail y shapp.” Tra va mee ayns shen, haink inneen veg stiagh marish e moir. Va laa ruggyree ec yn inneen. Hug Lowenna milljag beg jee, lesh “Laa ruggyree sonney!” screeuit er ayns shocklaid. Ren yn inneen mongey, as ren Lowenna mongey neesht.

My ta shiu er y straid vooar, gow-jee stiagh as gow-jee milljag.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n traa ta Lowenna girree?
T'ee girree ec queig er y chlag, as t'ee cur yn oghe er roish shey.
Cre'n fa ta Lowenna smarr ny claareyn?
T'ee smarr ny claareyn lesh eeym, ny bee'n teayst lhiantyn orroo.
Cre ta Lowenna cur er mullagh y milljag share eck?
T'ee cur ayrnyn beggey dy shelleig er mullagh y milljag.
Cre ta Lowenna screeu er dagh mynjeig?
T'ee screeu yn ennym as y prios er dagh mynjeig.
Cre hug Lowenna da'n inneen veg?
Hug ee milljag beg jee, lesh “Laa ruggyree sonney!” screeuit er.

lessons.title: Laa Illiam Dhone
lessons.summary: On the second of January the columnist joins a small crowd at a hill near Castletown with the historian Gaukroger Tulley, who tells the story of Illiam Dhone: in the time of the English republic he turned against the Earl's lady and gave the island to Parliament after only a skirmish or two, the king later granted a pardon to all, yet the new Earl tried Illiam for treason and had him shot; the king's council called it a shame, and people still ask whether he was a traitor or an honest man.
lessons.text:
Er yn nah laa jeh Jerrey Geuree, hie mee dys cronk beg rish y cheayn faggys da Balley Chashtal. Va sleih ayns shen, ayns y gheay feayr. Ta sleih çheet dys y chronk shoh dagh blein er y laa shoh, dy chooinaghtyn er Illiam Dhone. Va Gaukroger Tulley ayns shen neesht. T'eh screeu lioaryn shennaghys, as dinsh eh y skeeal dou.

“Va Illiam ny offishear mooar 'syn ellan ayns y 17oo eash,” dooyrt Gaukroger. “Ayns y traa shen, va caggey ayns Sostyn eddyr y ree as y parlamaid. Va caggaghyn mooarey ayns Sostyn, as skirmish dy chooilley laa. Ayns y jerrey, hooar y parlamaid yn varriaght, as va'n ree currit gys baase. Va Sostyn ny pobblaght rish tammylt.”

Cha row pobblaghtys mie lesh Eearley yn ellan. Va'n Eearley er ve caggey son y ree ayns Sostyn, as va eh currit gys baase myrgeddin. Va ben yn Eearley 'syn ellan foast. “Cha row Illiam er son pobblaghtys, foddee,” dooyrt Gaukroger. “Va eh smooinaghtyn er sleih yn ellan, as er y thalloo oc. Tra haink lhongyn y pharlamaid, hug Illiam as e gheiney yn ellan daue. Cha row caggey mooar ayn: cha row agh skirmish ny ghaa.”

Lurg jeih bleeaney, va ree noa ayns Lunnin, as hug eh pardoon da dy chooilley ghooinney v'er ve noi e ayr. Agh cha row yn Eearley noa laccal pardoon y chur da Illiam. Va Illiam goit, as va cassid traitoorys currit er. Dooyrt Illiam nagh row eh ny ghooinney traitooragh, as dy row pardoon y ree echey. Cha ren ny briwnyn clashtyn rish. Er yn nah laa jeh Jerrey Geuree 1663, va Illiam currit gys baase er y chronk shoh.

“Tra cheayll y ree mychione shen, va farg mooar er,” dooyrt Gaukroger. “Dooyrt quaiyl y ree dy row eh nearey son y briwnys, son dy row y pardoon reeoil ec Illiam. Va ny briwnyn kerrit. Ren y ree bronney thalloo Illiam er e lught-thie reesht. Agh va Illiam marroo.”

Hug mee yn feysht er Gaukroger: “Row eh ny ghooinney traitooragh, ny ny ghooinney ynrick?”

“Ta'n feysht shen ayn foast,” dooyrt eh. “Da'n Eearley, va Illiam traitooragh, as she traitoorys v'ayn. Da sleih yn ellan, va eh ynrick. Ren eh ny v'eh smooinaghtyn dy row kiart son yn ellan. Ta mee smooinaghtyn hene dy row eh ynrick, as dy row y briwnys ny nearey er yn Eearley.”

Ec y jerrey, ren y sleih arrane ayns Gaelg. Ren paitçhyn y valley bronney blaaghyn er y chlagh, myr t'ad jannoo dagh blein. Ta'n chlagh beg, as cha nel agh daa ockle er: “Illiam Dhone.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta sleih çheet dys y chronk er yn nah laa jeh Jerrey Geuree?
T'ad çheet dy chooinaghtyn er Illiam Dhone, son dy row eh currit gys baase ayns shen.
Row caggey mooar 'syn ellan tra haink lhongyn y pharlamaid?
Cha row. Cha row agh skirmish ny ghaa.
Cre hug y ree noa da sleih v'er ve noi e ayr?
Hug eh pardoon daue.
Cre dooyrt quaiyl y ree mychione y briwnys?
Dooyrt ee dy row eh nearey, son dy row y pardoon reeoil ec Illiam.
Vel Gaukroger smooinaghtyn dy row Illiam traitooragh?
Cha nel. T'eh smooinaghtyn dy row eh ynrick.

lessons.title: Benrein ayns y theater
lessons.summary: The columnist reviews a new play in the town theatre about Anne Boleyn and her daughter Elizabeth, seen from a cheap seat in the gallery: the young actress Tamsin Hocking is nervous at first but gives a powerful performance as a queen accused of adultery, the satin dresses shine, a musician plays a chromatic harmonica, the staging is cinematic, plague in London closes the theatres in one scene, and the play ends with Elizabeth, who kept her virginity and never married.
lessons.text:
Va mee ayns y theater 'sy valley Jeheiney shoh chaie, son y chied oie jeh cloie noa. Cha row argid aym son soiaghyn mie, myr shen va mee seose 'sy lout. Ta'n lout ard as ta ny soiaghyn creoi, agh ta'n ardan ry-akin dy mie veih'n lout, as cha nel tiggad 'sy lout agh queig punt.

Ta'n cloie mychione Anne Boleyn, nah ven Ree Inry, as mychione Ealisaid, yn inneen oc. Ta'n aghteyr aeg Tamsin Hocking cloie Anne. Ec y toshiaght, va Tamsin nearagh. Va'n chied ockle eck feer veg, as cha dod ad clashtyn rish 'sy lout. Ta dy chooilley aghteyr nearagh er y chied oie, foddee. Agh lurg tammylt, ren ee jarrood dy row ee nearagh, as v'ee feer niartallagh.

'Sy nah ayrn jeh'n chloie, ta Anne goit. Ta cassidyn currit urree: adultrinys, as traitoorys noi yn ree. Ta fys ec y sleih 'sy theater nagh vel ny cassidyn firrinagh. Cha nel Anne er jannoo adultrinys. Agh ta'n ree laccal ben noa, as ta adultrinys ny chassid aashagh. Ta Tamsin loayrt rish ny briwnyn ayns aght feer niartallagh. Ren ben ny hoie er my lhiattee keayney.

Ta ny gooynyn 'sy chloie jeant ass stroll. Ta stroll gial as bog, as ta'n soilshey cur er ny gooynyn stroll dy ve soilshagh myr ushtey. Ta gooyn stroll doo er Anne 'sy jerrey.

Ta kiaulleyder ny hassoo ec oirr yn ardan, as t'eh cloie harmoan cromaidagh. Ta kiaull y harmoan cromaidagh trimshagh as aalin. Cha row mee er chlashtyn harmoan cromaidagh ayns theater rieau.

Ta aght y chloie fillymagh. Ta'n soilshey goll veih boayl dys boayl myr ayns fillym, as ta caslyssyn er y voalley ny cooyl yn ardan. Ayns un ayrn, ta'n plaih ayns Lunnin, as ta ny theateryn dooint. Ta'n plaih jeant lesh soilshey ruy, as ta sleih goll marroo 'sy straid. She ayrn fillymagh as trimshagh eh. Cha nel mee er vakin plaih er ardan roie.

Ta'n cloie goll gys jerrey lesh Ealisaid. T'ee ny benrein nish. Ta ny deiney ooasle laccal dy jean ee poosey, agh ta Ealisaid gra dy vel ee poost rish yn ellan. Ta ny deiney loayrt mychione e moidynoilaght, as t'ee gra nagh vel e moidynoilaght cooish daue. Ren ny sleih 'sy lout gearey.

Ta'n cloie ry-akin dagh oie gys y Jesarn. Cha nel eh fillymagh ayns dy chooilley ayrn, agh t'eh mie. Ta mee gra rish dy chooilley lhaihder: gow-jee tiggad, as gow-jee soiagh 'sy lout.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va'n screeudeyr 'sy lout?
Cha row argid echey son soiaghyn mie, as cha nel tiggad 'sy lout agh queig punt.
Row Tamsin nearagh?
Va. Ec y toshiaght, va Tamsin nearagh, agh lurg tammylt v'ee feer niartallagh.
Cre ny cassidyn ta currit er Anne?
Ta adultrinys currit urree, as traitoorys noi yn ree.
Cre ta'n kiaulleyder cloie?
T'eh cloie harmoan cromaidagh.
Cre ta Ealisaid gra mychione e moidynoilaght?
T'ee gra nagh vel e moidynoilaght cooish daue.

lessons.title: Fo'n peamad
lessons.summary: Workers dig up the pavement on the Douglas promenade to change the old sewage pipes, and the columnist goes down with the engineer Hedley Lanyon: the excavation has found an old brick tunnel, the damp is so high that mushrooms grow on the walls, slime covers the old pipes, some parts are inaccessible to the machines so the men work by hand, and the partial closure of the road angers the shopkeepers until Hedley promises the pavement back before summer.
lessons.text:
Ta'n peamad er y raad rish y cheayn ayns Doolish ooilley brisht rish mee nish. Ta obbreeyn çheet dagh moghrey lesh jeshaghtyn mooarey, as t'ad gobbraghey veih shiaght er y chlag derrey shiaght 'syn astyr. Ta sleih y valley briaght dy chooilley laa: cre t'ad jannoo fo'n peamad?

Hie mee sheese dy akin. Ta Hedley Lanyon ny jeshaghteyr, as t'eh stiurey yn obbyr. “Ta ny feddanyn mooynlagh fo'n raad shoh keead as feed blein d'eash,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n mooynlagh veih ny thieyn as ny shappyn goll trooid ny feddanyn shoh gys y cheayn. Ta ny feddanyn brisht ayns ymmodee ynnydyn. Ta shin cur feddanyn noa sheese.”

Ren y toaghailt toshiaght ayns Mee Houney. Ec y toshiaght, hooar ad red nagh row fys oc er: thiollane shenn jeant ass breekyn, fo'n peamad. Ghow Hedley mee sheese 'syn thiollane lesh lampey. Va'n aer feayr as fliugh. “Ta'n tashid feer ard ayns shoh,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n tashid cur er ny breekyn dy ve bog, as ta red ennagh gaase er ny boallaghyn.”

Ren mee jeeaghyn. Va shalmaneyn beggey bane gaase er y voalley, as ymmodee jeu. “Ta shalmaneyn gaase ayns dy chooilley voayl dorraghey as fliugh,” dooyrt Hedley. “Cha nel ad mie dy ee, myrgeddin!”

Va ny shenn feddanyn coodit lesh sleetçh. Va'n sleetçh glass as doo, as va soar olk jeh. Hug Hedley e laue er y sleetçh, as ren eh gearey. “T'ou er gheddyn yn ayrn share jeh'n obbyr shoh,” dooyrt eh.

Ta ayrnyn jeh'n thiollane neuroshtynagh da ny jeshaghtyn: ta'n raad ro veg, as ro injil. Er-y-fa shen, ta ny deiney gobbraghey ayns ny ynnydyn neuroshtynagh lesh nyn laueyn, myr ren deiney roish keead as feed blein. Ta'n obbyr shen moal as creoi.

Ta'n raad dooint ayns ayrn: she dooney paartagh eh. Foddee gleashtanyn goll er un lhiattee jeh'n raad, agh cha nel kied ec gleashtanyn mooarey goll er yn lhiattee elley. Ta'n dooney paartagh cur farg er ny shellooderyn shappyn. “Cha nel ny turrysee çheet,” dooyrt ben ta creck arran 'sy straid.

Dooyrt Hedley dy bee'n toaghailt jeant roish y tourey. “Bee peamad noa er y raad roish Boaldyn,” dooyrt eh. “As bee feddanyn noa fo'n peamad, son keead blein elley.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta'n peamad brisht?
Ta ny obbreeyn cur feddanyn mooynlagh noa sheese, son dy vel ny shenn feddanyn brisht.
Cre hooar ad ec toshiaght y toaghailt?
Hooar ad thiollane shenn jeant ass breekyn fo'n peamad.
Cre va gaase er boallaghyn y thiollane?
Va shalmaneyn beggey bane gaase er ny boallaghyn, son dy vel y tashid ard.
Kys ta ny deiney gobbraghey ayns ny ynnydyn neuroshtynagh?
T'ad gobbraghey lesh nyn laueyn.
Cre'n fa ta farg er ny shellooderyn shappyn?
Ta farg orroo son dy vel dooney paartagh er y raad, as nagh vel ny turrysee çheet.

lessons.title: Yn thie eeast rish y phurt
lessons.summary: The columnist goes with a primary class to the small aquarium on the quay, where the keeper Gweniver Treganza shows a whale skeleton from a harmless minke whale, crabs and lobsters as crustaceans creeping on the floor of a tank, coral made of tiny polyps, a seal that finds fish with its whiskers, and a film about penguins that live on lava rocks at the equator in the Galapagos.
lessons.text:
Ta thie eeast beg rish y phurt 'sy valley, as hie mee ayn Jeheiney shoh chaie marish ynseyder as feed paitçhey veih'n vunscoill. She Gweniver Treganza freilleyder y thie eeast. T'ee gobbraghey ayn rish jeih bleeaney.

Ec y dorrys, ta ushylagh mooar croghey veih'n vullagh. She ushylagh whayl eh. “Va'n whayl shoh marroo er y traie rish Purt ny h-Inshey,” dooyrt Gweniver. “She whayl veg v'ayn. Ta whaylyn myr shoh neuskielleydagh. T'ad gee eeastyn beggey, as cha nel ad jannoo assee da sleih.” Va aggle er guilley beg roish y whayl. “Ta'n whayl neuskielleydagh,” dooyrt Gweniver rish, “as t'eh marroo myrgeddin!” Ren ny paitçhyn gearey, as cha row aggle er y guilley ny sodjey roish y whayl neuskielleydagh.

'Sy chied tank, va partanyn, as gimmagh mooar. “She crustee ad,” dooyrt Gweniver. “Ta bleayst creoi er dagh crustagh, as t'ad snaueaneagh: cha nel ad snaue myr eeastyn, agh t'ad goll er laare y tank er nyn gassyn.” Ren ny paitçhyn jeeaghyn er ny crustee snaueaneagh, goll dy moal veih creg dys creg.

'Sy nah tank, va corralagh as daaghyn ruy as bane er. “Ta ymmodee sleih smooinaghtyn dy vel corralagh ny chlagh,” dooyrt Gweniver. “Agh ta'n corralagh jeant ass pollypyn. She dooieyn beggey ad. Ta dagh pollyp feer veg, as ta thousaneyn jeh ny pollypyn cooidjagh jannoo y corralagh.”

Ayns y tank mooar, va raun. Va robaigyn liauyrey bane er e eddin. “Ta ny robaigyn feer scanshoil da'n raun,” dooyrt Gweniver. “'Syn ushtey dorraghey, cha nel y raun fakin monney. Agh ta ny robaigyn geddyn fys er yn ushtey gleashagh, as ta fys ec y raun c'raad ta ny eeastyn.” Hug ee eeast 'syn ushtey, as hooar y raun eh ayns un tullagh.

Ec y jerrey, hie ny paitçhyn stiagh ayns shamyr veg dy akin fillym mychione spennigyn. “Ta'n chooid smoo jeh ny spennigyn bio ayns ardjyn feayr,” dooyrt Gweniver, “agh ta spennigyn ennagh bio er ny h-Ellanyn Galapagos, ayns ardjyn meanchiarkylagh.” Ren ny paitçhyn jeeaghyn er ny spennigyn beggey er creggyn doo. “Ta ny creggyn shen jeant ass leavey,” dooyrt Gweniver. “Haink y leavey magh ass volcaanyn, as ren y leavey cur er ny ellanyn shen dy ve. Ta ny spennigyn shoh ny spennigyn meanchiarkylagh, as cha nel spennig elley erbee bio cha faggys da'n meanchiarkyl.”

Ren inneen veg briaght: “Vel y leavey çheh?” Ren Gweniver gearey. “Cha nel. T'eh feayr nish, as creoi. Agh ta'n ghrian çheh, as ta ny spennigyn goll 'syn ushtey son dy ve feayr.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta croghey veih'n vullagh ec y dorrys?
Ta ushylagh whayl croghey veih'n vullagh.
Cre'n fa ta ny crustee snaueaneagh?
Cha nel ad snaue myr eeastyn, agh t'ad goll er laare y tank er nyn gassyn.
Cre jeh ta'n corralagh jeant?
Ta'n corralagh jeant ass pollypyn, dooieyn beggey.
Cre'n fa ta ny robaigyn scanshoil da'n raun?
Ta ny robaigyn geddyn fys er yn ushtey gleashagh, as ta fys ec y raun c'raad ta ny eeastyn.
C'raad ta ny spennigyn meanchiarkylagh bio?
T'ad bio er ny h-Ellanyn Galapagos, er creggyn leavey.

lessons.title: Yn prentyr as y daan
lessons.summary: The columnist visits Peder Tresize, an old printer in a back street of Douglas who still prints by hand, while the calligrapher Ysella Ennor writes a Manx poem in calligraphy for a poster: they talk about the prosody of the poem, the hyphen in Manx words, dust particles that spoil a print, a smeared letter, Manx as a minority language, and a game of random words.
lessons.text:
Ayns straid veg cooyl y straid vooar ayns Doolish, ta shapp shenn lesh uinnag vooar. She shapp Peder Tresize eh. She prentyr Peder. T'eh three feed as jeih blein d'eash, as t'eh foast prent lesh e laueyn, er jeshaght veih'n nah eash jeig. “Ta prentyr erbee elley gobbraghey lesh co-earrooder nish,” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel agh un prentyr myr mish 'syn ellan, as she prentyr shenn mish.”

Er y laa va mee ayns shen, va Ysella Ennor ayns y shapp neesht. She ben penneyrys ee: t'ee screeu lettyryn aalin lesh penn as doo. Ta penneyrys myr ellyn. Va Ysella screeu daan Gaelg son caslys mooar, as va Peder goll dy yannoo keead coip jeh.

Ren Ysella lhaih yn daan dou. “Ta prosoid y daan shoh feer vie,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n trimmid er y chied shillab jeh dy chooilley ockle, myr ta dy kinjagh 'sy Ghaelg. Tra ta mee screeu yn daan lesh penneyrys, ta mee freayll yn prosoid 'sy cheeayl: ta lettyryn mooarey er ny shillabyn trome.”

Ta schimmeig ayns ymmodee focklyn 'sy Ghaelg: lught-thie, myr sampleyr. “Ta'n schimmeig doillee 'sy phenneyrys,” dooyrt Ysella. “My ta'n schimmeig ro liauyr, ta'n ockle jeeaghyn myr daa ockle.”

Hug Peder ny lettyryn fuygh 'sy jeshaght. Roish my ren eh prent, ren eh glenney yn jeshaght lesh eaddagh. “Ta partigalyn beggey dy joan ayns dy chooilley voayl,” dooyrt eh. “Foddee un partigal er y phabyr cowrey bane y yannoo er y choip.” Va'n chied choip mie, agh va lettyr ny ghaa smearit. “Ta'n doo ro hiu,” dooyrt Peder. “Ta'n lettyr smearit son dy vel doo ro vooar er.” Ren eh y doo y ghlenney, as cha row lettyr smearit erbee 'sy nah choip.

Va'n daan mychione y Ghaelg hene. “She mynçhengey yn Ghaelg,” dooyrt Ysella. “Ta feme ec mynçhengey er sleih ta screeu ee as loayrt ee dy chooilley laa. Ta caslys aalin cur er sleih jeeaghyn er y Ghaelg.” Dooyrt Peder dy row e vac-y-mac goll dys bunscoill raad ta ny paitçhyn ynsaghey ayns Gaelg, as nagh row mynçhengey erbee cha bio 'syn ellan.

Ec y jerrey, haink mac-y-mac Peder stiagh. Ren eh cloie gamman: ghow eh lettyryn skelimagh ass y kishtey, as ren eh fockle jeu. “Ta ny lettyryn skelimagh,” dooyrt eh, “agh ta'n fockle firrinagh!” Ren ny lettyryn skelimagh yn fockle “mie”.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta Peder prentyr er lheh?
T'eh foast prent lesh e laueyn, er jeshaght shenn.
Cre ta Ysella jannoo lesh penneyrys?
T'ee screeu daan Gaelg son caslys mooar.
C'raad ta'n trimmid ayns prosoid y daan?
Ta'n trimmid er y chied shillab jeh dy chooilley ockle.
Cre'n fa ren Peder glenney yn jeshaght?
Son dy vel partigalyn beggey dy joan ayns dy chooilley voayl, as foddee un partigal cowrey bane y yannoo.
Cre'n fa va lettyr ny ghaa smearit?
Va doo ro vooar er ny lettyryn.

lessons.title: Laa ayns y çhaplynys
lessons.summary: The columnist spends a day with Bersaba Polwarth, who runs the chaplaincy in the town hospital: she visits an uneasy old fisherman before an operation and listens to his worry, sits with a young blood donor who feels faint, calls the synagogue so that a rabbi can visit a patient, explains that penance is not her work but a priest's, and says that compassion matters more than medical knowledge.
lessons.text:
Ta shamyr veg ayns y lheelann 'sy valley, faggys da'n dorrys mooar. Ta “Çhaplynys” screeuit er y dorrys. She shoh ynnyd Bersaba Polwarth. T'ee stiurey yn çhaplynys rish hoght bleeaney. Ta'n çhaplynys son dy chooilley ghooinney: son sleih lesh credjue, as son sleih gyn credjue erbee.

Hie mee marish Bersaba son un laa. Ec nuy er y chlag, hie shin dys lhiabbee shenn eeasteyr enmyssit Ffinlo. Va obbraid echey 'syn astyr. Va Ffinlo neuaashagh. Cha row eh abyl lhie dy aashagh, as va e laueyn gleashagh. “Ta imnea orrym,” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel mee er ve ayns lheelann rieau.” Ren Bersaba soie sheese, as ren ee clashtyn rish e imnea son lieh oor. Cha dooyrt ee monney. Tra va shin faagail, va Ffinlo ny s'aashagh, as cha row eh cha neuaashagh.

Ec yn eanish, hie shin dys y shamyr raad ta sleih cur fuill. Va guilley aeg ayns shen, cur fuill son y chied cheayrt. “She toyrtyssagh fuill mie eh,” dooyrt yn boandyr, “agh t'eh jeeaghyn bane.” Ren Bersaba soie rish y toyrtyssagh aeg, as hug ee cappan tey da. “Ta ymmodee sleih çheet er-ash dy chur fuill reesht,” dooyrt Bersaba. “Ta feme ec y lheelann er dy chooilley toyrtyssagh.”

'Syn astyr, va ben aeg ayns lhiabbee ayns shamyr elley. Ta'n ven aeg goll dys y synagogue dagh shiaghtin, as va laccal eck dy loayrt rish rabbi. Cha nel rabbi ayns y lheelann, agh hug Bersaba fys dys y synagogue 'sy valley. Ta'n synagogue beg, agh ta'n sleih ayn feer chairys. Haink y rabbi lurg oor.

Ta sleih briaght jeh Bersaba mychione pennys neesht. “Laa ennagh, dooyrt ben dou dy row ee laccal pennys son peccah shenn,” dooyrt Bersaba. “Agh cha nel pennys ny obbyr aym. She obbyr saggyrt eh. Hug mee fys er y saggyrt eck. Ta mee hene clashtyn, guee, as soie marish sleih.”

Ta fys lheihyssagh ec Bersaba myrgeddin: v'ee ny boandyr roish my ren ee goaill toshiaght 'sy çhaplynys. “Ta ny lheeyn as ny boandyryn cur kiarail lheihyssagh da'n chorp,” dooyrt ee. “Agh cha nel fys lheihyssagh dy liooar. Ta feme ec sleih er çhymmey. Ta çhymmey ny smoo scanshoil na red erbee.”

Ec shiaght er y chlag, hie shin er-ash dys Ffinlo. Va'n obbraid jeant, as va Ffinlo mongey. “Ren oo clashtyn rish my imnea,” dooyrt eh rish Bersaba. “Va dty çhymmey feer vie dou.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta'n çhaplynys son?
Ta'n çhaplynys son dy chooilley ghooinney, lesh credjue ny gyn credjue.
Cre'n fa va Ffinlo neuaashagh?
Va imnea er roish yn obbraid, son nagh row eh er ve ayns lheelann rieau.
Cre ren Bersaba son y toyrtyssagh aeg?
Ren ee soie rish, as hug ee cappan tey da.
Cre'n fa hug Bersaba fys dys y synagogue?
Va'n ven aeg laccal loayrt rish rabbi.
Cre ta ny smoo scanshoil na fys lheihyssagh, rere Bersaba?
Ta çhymmey ny smoo scanshoil na red erbee.

lessons.title: Oie ny çhentagyn
lessons.summary: On fireworks night the columnist takes her son Breward to the promenade and leaves the old dog Bunty at home: the aerial fireworks are incredible and the spinning wheels throw shadows on the houses, but at home Bunty has run off in fear; after a long search she finds him wandering on the beach, he scratches at the door to come in, and she makes him a comfortable bed under the stairs.
lessons.text:
Dagh blein 'sy gheurey, ta çhentagyn er y raad rish y cheayn 'sy valley. Ta thousaneyn dy leih çheet dy akin ad. Er y vlein shoh, hie mee marish my vac Breward. T'eh shiaght bleeaney d'eash, as va'n chied cheayrt echey. Daag shin y shenn voddey ain, Bunty, 'sy thie, son dy vel aggle echey roish çhentagyn.

Va ny çhentagyn speyragh neuchredjallagh. Hie ny roggadyn seose ard 'syn aer, as eisht va soilshey ruy, glass as airh ayns dy chooilley voayl. “Jeeagh er shid!” dooyrt Breward, as eh soilshaghey seose. Va çhentag speyragh vooar ayns shid, er y cheayn, myr blaa jeant ass aile. Cha row Breward er vakin red cha neuchredjallagh rieau. “T'ad neuchredjallagh!” dooyrt eh dy kinjagh.

Er y thalloo, va queeylyn çhentag sneeu. Ta queeyl sneeu cur magh aile as soilshey ayns dy chooilley raad. Tra va ny queeylyn sneeu, va scadooyn liauyrey er boallaghyn ny thieyn, as va ny scadooyn gleashagh myr sleih ec daunsey. Ren Breward gearey, as ren eh cloie lesh e scadoo hene er y peamad.

Tra haink shin er-ash dys y thie, va'n dorrys foshlit, as cha row Bunty ayn. Va'n dorrys er ve foshlit liorish y gheay. Va aggle orrym. Hie shin magh dy hirrey er Bunty. Va'n oie dorraghey, as va çhentagyn foast ry-chlashtyn ayns shid, er y cheayn.

Lurg oor, honnick shin Bunty er y traie, rouail veih creg dys creg. V'eh er ve rouail rish oor, foddee, lesh aggle er. Cha daink eh hooin tra deie shin er. Agh tra va ny çhentagyn ooilley jeant, haink eh er-ash dys y thie e unnane. Ren eh scrob er y dorrys, myr t'eh jannoo dagh oie. Cheayll shin eh scrob er y fuygh, as ren mee yn dorrys y osley. Va cowraghyn er y dorrys veih ny keayrtyn elley t'eh er scrob er.

Va Bunty fliugh as feayr, as va aggle er foast. Ren mee lhiabbee soccaragh da fo ny greeishyn, lesh shenn eaddagh bog. Ta'n boayl shen dorraghey, as cha nel ny çhentagyn ry-chlashtyn ayn. Ren Bunty lhie sheese 'sy lhiabbee soccaragh, as v'eh ny chadley ayns tullagh.

Er y vlein elley, hed Breward dys ny çhentagyn marish e ayr. Bee mee 'sy thie marish Bunty, ayns boayl soccaragh, as cha bee eh rouail er y traie reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa daag ad Bunty 'sy thie?
Ta aggle echey roish çhentagyn.
Cre honnick Breward ayns shid, er y cheayn?
Honnick eh çhentag speyragh vooar, myr blaa jeant ass aile.
Cre ren ny queeylyn sneeu er boallaghyn ny thieyn?
Ren ad scadooyn liauyrey, as va ny scadooyn gleashagh.
C'raad hooar ad Bunty?
Honnick ad Bunty er y traie, rouail veih creg dys creg.
Cre ren yn screeudeyr son Bunty?
Ren ee lhiabbee soccaragh da fo ny greeishyn.

lessons.title: Quaaltys rish y fer-drigey
lessons.summary: The columnist interviews Mawgan Trethowan, once the singer of a punk band in Douglas and now distils strong drink in an old warehouse by the harbour: he speaks of punk, of the prototype still he built from an old copper pot, of the poteen his grandfather made on a farm, of quinine in tonic water, and of people who called his plan nonsense, and he asks for his answers to be printed short and concise.
lessons.text:
Ta mee screeu quaaltys 'sy cholloo shoh dagh mee. Er y vee shoh, ren mee quaaltys rish Mawgan Trethowan. Feed blein er dy henney, v'eh arraneyder ayns possan sponk ayns Doolish. Nish t'eh drigey jough ayns shenn stoyr rish y phurt.

Hie mee stiagh 'sy stoyr. Va sthill mooar jeant ass prash ayns mean y laare, as va soar millish 'syn aer. Va Mawgan ny hassoo rish y sthill, lesh e folt liauyr glass. Hoshee mee yn quaaltys lesh feysht er sponk.

“V'ou ayns possan sponk. Vel sponk ayns dty vea foast?”

“Ta,” dooyrt eh. “Va sponk mychione jannoo dty red hene, gyn cur fys er sleih elley. Cha row monney argid ain, agh ren shin arraneyn as kiaull nyn lomarcan. Ta mee jannoo yn obbyr shoh myr shen neesht.”

“C'raad hooar oo yn sthill?”

“Cha nel y sthill shoh agh yn nah sthill. Va'n chied sthill ny frauehoylley: ren mee eh ass shenn pott prash 'sy garey ec my voir. Va'n frauehoylley beg as olk, agh dynsee mee ymmodee reddyn veih. Lurg y frauehoylley, ren fer-obbree sthill mooar dou ayns Nalbin.”

“Row drigey ayns dty lught-thie roish?”

Ren Mawgan gearey. “Va. Ren my shenn-ayr poteen er y thalloo echey. Va'n poteen noi yn leigh, as v'eh drigit ayns sthill beg ayns cooyl y thie. Ta skeealyn ayn mychione poteen as y poleen, agh cha dooar ad rieau y sthill echey!”

“Cre ta sleih giu marish dty yough?”

“Ushtey sharroo, son y chooid smoo. Ta quineen ayns yn ushtey shen: shen ta cur yn blass sharroo da. Ayns shenn laghyn, va quineen ny lheihys noi malaarey. Ren sidooryn ayns ardjyn çheh giu quineen marish jough son dy ve slane.”

“Row sleih gra nagh jinnagh oo gobbraghey?”

“Va. Dooyrt ymmodee sleih dy row eh ommidjys: arraneyder sponk jannoo jough! Dooyrt my vanc dy row eh ommidjys neesht. Nish, cha nel fer erbee gra ommidjys. Ta mee creck boteilyn er y gherrey dys Sostyn as Nerin.”

Ec y jerrey, ren Mawgan briaght orrym: “Vod oo my freggyrtyn y screeu cumir? Cha mie lhiam focklyn ro liauyr.” Myr shen, ta ny freggyrtyn echey ayns y cholloo shoh cumir. Cha nel mee er screeu agh ny reddyn scanshoil.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va Mawgan feed blein er dy henney?
V'eh arraneyder ayns possan sponk ayns Doolish.
Cre va'n chied sthill echey?
Va'n chied sthill ny frauehoylley jeant ass shenn pott prash.
Quoi ren poteen?
Ren shenn-ayr Mawgan poteen er y thalloo echey.
Cre'n fa ta ushtey sharroo sharroo?
Ta quineen ayn, as ta'n quineen cur yn blass sharroo da.
Cre'n fa ta ny freggyrtyn ayns y cholloo cumir?
Ren Mawgan briaght er y screeudeyr dy screeu ny freggyrtyn echey cumir.

lessons.title: Yn plan son y margey
lessons.summary: The columnist sits through a town council meeting about the renewal of the old market square: the councillor Elowen Trebarwith presents the plan in its entirety, with a glass market hall under a pyramidal roof and a car park on arable land at the edge of town; the farmer Hammett Tremenheere calls the plan destructive for the old trees where nuthatches nest, one councillor's reasoning is clear and another's argument is irrational, and the council votes to keep the trees and the field.
lessons.text:
Jeheiney shoh chaie, va cruinnaght jeh coonseil y valley, as va mee ayns shen son y cholloo shoh. Va'n chooish mychione aanoaghey y shenn vargey. Ta'n margey ayns mean y valley rish keead blein, agh ta ny thieyn mygeayrt-y-mysh eh shenn as brisht. Ta'n coonseil laccal aanoaghey yn ynnyd ooilley.

Hoshee yn coonseilagh Elowen Trebarwith lesh y plan. Hug ee y plan 'sy slanid echey er scaailan mooar, son dy row ee laccal dy jinnagh dy chooilley pheiagh fakin y slanid jeh, as cha nel ayrnyn jeh ynrican. Ta thie margee noa ayns y plan, jeant ass glonney, lesh mullagh pyramidoil. “Ta'n mullagh pyramidoil cur soilshey stiagh veih dy chooilley lhiattee,” dooyrt Elowen. “Bee eh ry-akin veih'n cheayn.”

Ta boayl son gleashtanyn ayns y plan neesht, er oirr y valley. Agh ta'n boayl shen ny thalloo traauoil. Ta Hammett Tremenheere ny eirinagh, as t'eh freayll y thalloo traauoil shen rish daeed blein. T'eh soiaghey oarn ayn dagh blein. Hass eh seose. “Cha nel monney thalloo traauoil faggys da'n valley,” dooyrt eh. “My ta shiu cur gleashtanyn er, cha bee eh traauoil dy bragh reesht.”

Dooyrt Hammett myrgeddin dy row y plan traartagh son y pairk beg rish y margey. Ta biljyn shenn ayns y pairk, as ta'n plan giarrey sheese ad. “Ta'n plan traartagh,” dooyrt eh. “Ta red erbee ta traartagh son biljyn traartagh son ushagyn neesht. Ta'n scolteyder croiyn bio 'sy phairk shen. Ta'n scolteyder croiyn ushag veg ghorrym, as t'ee jannoo e edd ayns towl ayns billey shenn. My ta ny biljyn goll, hed y scolteyder croiyn neesht.”

Va resoonaghey Hammett glen as jeeragh, as ren ymmodee sleih moylley yn resoonaghey echey. Eisht hass coonseilagh elley seose. “Ta ushagyn ayns dy chooilley voayl,” dooyrt eh. “My ta shin freayll dy chooilley villey son ushag, cha bee red noa erbee 'sy valley shoh. As ta'n ushag shen beg; cha nod eh ve scanshoil.” Va'n argane echey neuresoonagh. Cha nel ushag ny sloo scanshoil son dy vel ee beg. Dooyrt Elowen hene dy row yn argane shen neuresoonagh.

Ec y jerrey, va vote ayn. Ren y coonseil y plan y ghoaill 'sy slanid echey, agh lesh daa chaghlaa: bee ny biljyn shenn 'sy phairk freilt, as bee'n boayl son gleashtanyn ayns shenn stoyr, cha nel er y thalloo traauoil. Bee yn aanoaghey goaill toshiaght 'sy tourey. Lurg y chruinnaght, honnick mee Hammett ec y dorrys. “Va'n resoonaghey ayd mie,” dooyrt mee. Ren eh mongey. “Cha nel eh aym,” dooyrt eh. “She resoonaghey yn ushag veg eh.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta'n coonseil laccal jannoo lesh y shenn vargey?
T'ad laccal aanoaghey yn ynnyd ooilley.
Cre ta ayns y plan son y thie margee noa?
Ta thie margee jeant ass glonney ayns y plan, lesh mullagh pyramidoil.
Cre'n fa ta Hammett noi yn boayl son gleashtanyn?
Son dy vel y boayl shen ny thalloo traauoil, as cha bee eh traauoil dy bragh reesht.
C'raad ta'n scolteyder croiyn jannoo e edd?
T'ee jannoo e edd ayns towl ayns billey shenn.
Cre'n fa va argane y choonseilagh elley neuresoonagh?
Cha nel ushag ny sloo scanshoil son dy vel ee beg.
